title: Thread Synchronization with Locks and Queues
learningObjectives: Explain Lock, RLock, Event, Queue and producer-consumer coordination.
Select a suitable concurrency or performance technique for PY22.13.
Interpret task, thread, process or profiling results correctly.
Identify limitations and risks when applying PY22.13.
Apply PY22.13 concepts in maintainable Python code.

understand.concept: Thread synchronization coordinates access to shared resources and communication between threads. Lock protects a critical section, RLock allows the owning thread to acquire the same lock recursively, Event signals a condition and Queue safely transfers items between producers and consumers. Use the simplest primitive that matches the coordination requirement.
understand.whyItMatters: Correct synchronization prevents race conditions, lost updates and unsafe shared-state access.
understand.analogy: A lock is a single key to a shared room; a queue is a handoff tray where one worker leaves tasks for another.
understand.analogyLimit: Incorrect lock ordering can cause deadlocks, and holding locks during slow operations can reduce concurrency.
understand.summary: Thread Synchronization with Locks and Queues develops advanced concurrency and performance skills.

explain.narrative:
## Coordinate shared work
Use `threading.Lock` around short critical sections that access shared state. `RLock` supports recursive acquisition by the same thread. `Event` lets one thread signal another, and `queue.Queue` provides thread-safe producer-consumer communication.

Keep lock scopes small, release locks using a with statement and avoid acquiring multiple locks in inconsistent orders. Prefer queues for passing work rather than sharing complex mutable objects between threads.

examples.title: Use a lock context manager
examples.code:
import threading
lock = threading.Lock()
with lock:
    acquired = lock.locked()
print(acquired, lock.locked())
examples.explanation: The with statement releases the lock when the block exits.

examples.title: Transfer items through a queue
examples.code:
import queue
items = queue.Queue()
items.put('task-1')
print(items.get())

examples.title: Signal an event
examples.code:
import threading
event = threading.Event()
print(event.is_set())
event.set()
print(event.is_set())
examples.explanation: Event stores a flag that other threads can wait for.

examples.title: Check recursive lock type
examples.code:
import threading
lock = threading.RLock()
with lock:
    with lock: result = lock._is_owned()
print(result)
examples.explanation: RLock permits the owning thread to acquire the same lock recursively.

examples.title: Mark queue work as complete
examples.code:
import queue
items = queue.Queue()
items.put(1)
value = items.get()
items.task_done()
items.join()
print(value)
examples.explanation: task_done and join track completion of queued tasks.
